evidence.claim: The toolkit includes a magnetized case with sorting-tray lid, 150 mm flex extension, 4 mm aluminum bit driver, 4 mm screwdriver bits and adapter, anti-static wrist strap, suction handle, three opening tools, six opening picks, three types of tweezers, three spudgers, Jimmy, magnetic pad, and polyester tool roll.
evidence.verbatim:
- Easy-to-Open Magnetized Case
  - Apply opposing pressure to the top and bottom sides of the case (like opening a jar)
- Lid with Built-in Sorting Tray
- 150 mm Flex Extension
  - Used to get to those hard-to-reach screws
  - The bits are held in with friction
    - Please reference [this answer](/Answers/View/595946/Can+anyone+tell+me+how+do+I+use+the+flex+extension) for additional help
    - Also, note that the screws will not be held to the bit due the to friction system and not magnetic
      - The bits however can be magnetized with a magnetizer/demagnetizer if that functionality is desired and that can be [purchased here](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/magnetizer-demagnetizer)
- 4 mm Aluminum Bit Driver
  - This is not a pry tool
  - The magnetic bit holder transmits magnetism through the screwdriver bit, helping you handle all those tiny screws.
  - If you are experiencing any issues with the rotating end of the driver please reference the fixes in [this guide](/Guide/How+to+Reattach+the+Cap+on+a+4+mm+iFixit+Precision+Bit+Driver/145856).
- 4 mm Screwdriver Bits
  - For rust prevention, store the toolkit in a well-ventilated dry place indoors. Avoid prolonged exposure to humid, wet environments.
    - If you live in a humid wet environment (or anywhere) then utilize the desiccant bag that comes inside the bit case and add a few more for good measure
  - For rust removal: A bath with vinegar or Evapo-Rust or something along those lines works pretty well. After de-rusting a coating of oil should be re-applied, silicone spray, WD-40, spray wax, or anything to keep the elements off the surface of the material.
  - 1/4" to 4 mm Driver Adapter
    - The bits are held in with friction
      - Please reference [this guide](https://help.ifixit.com/article/188-64-bit-driver-kits-150mm-flexible-extension-is-not-holding-bits) for additional help.
      - Also, note that the screws will not be held to the bit due the to friction system and not magnetic
        - The bits however can be magnetized with a magnetizer/demagnetizer if that functionality is desired and that can be [purchased here](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/magnetizer-demagnetizer)
- Anti-Static Wrist Strap
  - Helps protect your electronics from accidental electrostatic discharge (ESD) damage during repairs.
  - The anti-static wrist strap is not designed to be conductive. In fact, it is designed to do the exact opposite of conducting static electricity, as wearing a conductive component during electronic repairs would more likely allow electrostatic discharge to harm your device.
  - It is designed to be highly resistant to anti-static buildup when used in conjunction with a ground, and it will protect your electronics from electrostatic discharge damage during repairs when worn and used in conjunction with a ground
  - We have [this guide](/Guide/How+to+Use+the+Anti-Static+Wrist+Strap/153022) detailing how to use this wrist strap
- Suction Handle
  - Works best under a warmer environment. When too cold the plastic suction portion becomes stiff and harder to adhere.
    - Even in a cold environment, the suction handle can be warmed up from the heat of your hands (or putting it in your pocket, or under an iOpener).
  - Works best on a smooth, flat glass surface. Cracked/shattered screens may pose difficulty in obtaining adequate suction. If your screen is cracked/shattered and suction cannot be obtained, [try this trick instead](/Guide/iPhone+SE+2020+Screen+Replacement/133817#s193571), using tape.
- 3x iFixit Opening Tool
  - Tough-yet-soft material pry open the tightest cracks, but won't scratch or mar your workpiece
  - Two tips provide alternate opening options: Wedge for breaching and Hook for lifting and levering
  - These tools are designed to break before the device does
  - Consumable - not covered under warranty
  - Can be purchased here [iFixit Opening Tool](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/ifixit-opening-tool)
  - [Watch video here](https://vimeo.com/176377498?embedded=true&source=vimeo_logo&owner=2326705)
- 6x iFixit Opening Pick
  - Can be used for prying, sliding, separating, and air guitaring.
  - These tools are designed to break before the device does
  - Consumable - not covered under warranty
  - Can be purchased here [6x iFixit Opening Pick](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/ifixit-opening-picks-set-of-6)
- Nylon Tipped Reverse Tweezers
  - ESD-safe nylon tips (the metal handle is not ESD-safe)
  - Reverse tweezers stay closed until you squeeze them open
  - Tips are replaceable and come in 3 types ([Pointed](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/nylon-tipped-tweezers?variant=31917884375121), [Blunt](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/nylon-tipped-tweezers?variant=31917884342353), [Curved](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/nylon-tipped-tweezers?variant=31917884309585))
  - Tweezers and tweezer tips have Lifetime Guarantee
- Angled ESD Tweezers
  - ESD safe
    - But shouldn't be used on live circuits. There won't be any transmission between the user's hand and the metallic tips, but the metallic nature of the tweezers means that they are electrically conductive from tip to tip.
  - With angled, pointed tips for hard-to-reach places
  - It comes with a small cap to cover the point that is consumable and not covered under warranty
  - If you notice the cap splitting you can reinforce it with some tape
- Blunt ESD Tweezers
  - ESD safe
    - But shouldn't be used on live circuits. There won't be any transmission between the user's hand and the metallic tips, but the metallic nature of the tweezers means that they are electrically conductive from tip to tip.
  - Blunted tips for powerful precision work.
  - It comes with a small cap to cover the point that is consumable and not covered under warranty
  - If you notice the cap splitting you can reinforce it with some tape
- Spudger
  - Poke and pry ask much as you like with this spudger
  - The tool also includes a notch for hooking wires.
  - The glass-filled nylon Spudger is the preferred spudger for use while soldering.
  - The pliable and antistatic properties make it ideal for working around sensitive electronic components without fear of shocking or scratching them (ESD safe)
  - This tool is designed to break before the device does
  - Consumable - not covered under warranty
  - Can be purchased here [Spudger](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/spudger?variant=31946524229713)
- Halberd Spudger
  - Specifically shaped for electronics repair, this spudger features a hook for scooping, scraping, pulling, and guiding.
  - ESD-safe fiber-reinforced nylon
  - This tool is designed to break before the device does
  - Consumable - not covered under warranty
  - Can be purchased here [Halberd Spudger](https://www.ifixit.com/en-eu/products/halberd-spudger)
- Metal Spudger
  - The ultimate prying tool for if you need a little more power than the opening tools can provide
  - Be sure to exercise caution when using this tool. With its great strength comes the potential to scratch or otherwise damage components
  - [Watch video here](https://vimeo.com/65236137?embedded=true&source=vimeo_logo&owner=2326705)
- Jimmy
  - A high-quality steel blade easily slips between the tightest gaps in the toughest devices.
  - [Watch video here](https://vimeo.com/105270399?embedded=true&source=vimeo_logo&owner=2326705)
  - Can be very sharp
  - Often times can not be taken on a plane, please [read this blog post](https://www.ifixit.com/News/32644/can-you-bring-ifixit-toolkits-on-a-plane) if you intend to travel with your Pro Tech Toolkit
- Magnetic Pad
  - Holds the bit case to the tool roll
  - If you are dealing with lots of screws or you don't want the screws to move around this pad can also hold onto those screws for you
- Tool Roll
  - Made of polyester with hook and loop (velcro) closure

assets.title: Where do the screws go after they come out?
assets.content:
Subject: Where do the screws go after they come out?
Preview text: The Pro Tech Toolkit’s removable magnetic lid gives them a defined place during disassembly.

Turn the case lid into a sorting surface

Hi there,

Give removed screws a dedicated surface while you work. The iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit lets you use the inside of its driver-kit lid as a sorting tray during disassembly.

The lid attaches magnetically to the driver-kit case. Remove it, turn it over, and you have a defined place to arrange fasteners instead of treating the case as packaging that sits aside.

When the work is done, the magnetic case and foam insert provide secure tool storage. The included fabric roll makes the broader toolkit portable, so the same design supports work at the bench and carrying the tools elsewhere.

A sorting surface does not record where each screw belongs, so careful tracking still matters. Visit the product page to decide whether the integrated tray and organized storage fit the way you want to work.

See the case and storage design →

- iFixit

Subject: What the Lifetime Guarantee covers
Preview text: See the defined promise—and the exclusions—before choosing your first general toolkit.

Know what lifetime coverage means

Hi there,

The Pro Tech Toolkit’s product page identifies a Lifetime Guarantee. iFixit defines that promise clearly: the covered product is guaranteed to function for as long as you have it.

That gives you a documented standard to consider when choosing a repair toolkit—not simply a durability claim with no stated duration.

The guarantee has boundaries. Claims may be denied for abuse, negligence, unintended use, cosmetic issues, loss, installation damage, accidental damage, misuse, device damage, or data loss. iFixit may also require the product to be returned for analysis before issuing credit or a replacement.

The iFixit Pro Tech Toolkit is a general repair toolkit with lifetime coverage identified on its product page. Review that label to decide whether the defined protection addresses your concern about covered tool failure during intended use.

Review the Lifetime Guarantee →

- iFixit

brief.interpretation: A pre-purchase nurture sequence for solution-aware, opted-in electronics hobbyists choosing their first broad repair toolkit—not customer onboarding. The sequence helps them judge fit, understand one practical use, and evaluate durability coverage before buying.
brief.reader:
Selected audience (user-stated constraints): Opted-in electronics hobbyists considering their first general repair toolkit.
No further recipient situation is established. Compiled market context is research to check for applicability, not a replacement biography.
brief.reader_segment: A hands-on electronics owner who is tired of improvising tools across phones, laptops, consoles, and household devices
brief.reader_profile_override: Opted-in electronics hobbyists considering their first general repair toolkit
brief.promise: The Pro Tech Toolkit is a broad, organized option for hobbyists who want one toolkit for varied electronics work, with practical repair tools and defined long-term coverage.
brief.orientation: The Pro Tech Toolkit is a general electronics repair kit combining a 64-bit driver set with opening, prying, gripping, and anti-static tools in portable storage.
brief.arc: First establish whether the toolkit's breadth matches the reader's likely repair range; then make that breadth tangible through one concrete project-management use; finally address concern about buying tools that may not last.
brief.sequence_rationale: The reader must determine relevance before tool details or guarantee terms matter. Email 1 therefore frames a fit test around device range and tool breadth. Email 2 turns the product from an inventory list into a concrete repair-workflow example. Email 3 resolves the supported durability concern with the Lifetime Guarantee and its limits. Each email can be understood independently and sends the reader to the same product page for the decision relevant to that message.

emails.job: Help the reader decide whether the Pro Tech Toolkit's breadth fits the kinds of electronics repairs they want to attempt.
emails.single_idea: The Pro Tech Toolkit is a fit when the reader wants coverage across several electronics categories and expects projects to require opening, prying, gripping, or anti-static tools as well as screwdriver bits.
emails.felt_need: I want one first toolkit that can stay useful across different electronics, but I do not want to buy breadth I will never use.
emails.status_quo: The reader may be comparing smaller bit sets, basic phone-and-laptop kits, or a broader general repair toolkit.
emails.why_it_fails: Bit count alone does not show whether a kit supports the non-screw steps that electronics repairs can involve.
emails.mechanism: The Pro Tech Toolkit combines 64 bits with tweezers, spudgers, opening tools, and anti-static accessories, and its stated device range includes electronics, gaming consoles, drones, RC cars, and vintage devices.
emails.belief_shift: Before: a larger toolkit may simply mean more bits. After: fit depends on both fastener breadth and whether the included handling and opening tools match the reader's intended repair work.
must_not_say: Do not claim the toolkit fits every device, model, or repair.
Do not imply that every reader's existing tools are inadequate.
Do not promise successful repairs or protection from device damage.
Do not introduce professional-repair or repair-business positioning.
Do not turn the email into a complete inventory list.
emails.objection: I cannot tell whether a 64-bit general toolkit is useful breadth or more kit than my first repairs require.
emails.call_to_action: View the Pro Tech Toolkit product page: https://www.ifixit.com/products/pro-tech-toolkit
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the included bit range and non-driver tools match the categories and repair steps the reader expects to encounter.
emails.next_step_value: The page lets the reader inspect the 64-bit driver kit, broader repair-tool assortment, and supported device range before choosing.
emails.next_step_limit: The page's general device range does not establish compatibility with every specific model or confirm every tool required by an individual repair guide.
emails.subject_strategy: Frame the open around a quick fit check for varied electronics work, not a sweeping claim that more tools are automatically better.

emails.job: Show one concrete way the toolkit supports an electronics repair after the device has been opened.
emails.single_idea: During disassembly, the inside of the driver-kit lid can serve as a sorting tray for removed fasteners while the case and foam insert keep the toolkit organized.
emails.felt_need: Once screws start coming out, I need a clear place to set them while I work.
emails.status_quo: A first-time toolkit buyer may focus on which bits remove screws without considering where those fasteners go during the repair.
emails.why_it_fails: Removing a fastener and managing it during disassembly are separate parts of the same task.
emails.mechanism: The driver-kit case uses a magnetically attached lid whose inside serves as a sorting tray; the broader toolkit uses a magnetic case, foam insert, and fabric roll for storage and portability.
emails.belief_shift: Before: the case is only packaging for the tools. After: part of the case becomes a usable work surface during disassembly, then returns to organized storage.
must_not_say: Do not claim the tray guarantees that screws cannot be lost or mixed up.
Do not claim the lid documents screw positions or replaces deliberate organization.
Do not broaden the email into a list of all 64 bits or every included tool.
Do not guarantee a repair outcome or imply that organization prevents device damage.
Do not invent a repair the recipient has already attempted.
emails.objection: A tool case may seem like storage that adds little once the repair begins.
emails.call_to_action: See the Pro Tech Toolkit's case and storage design on the product page: https://www.ifixit.com/products/pro-tech-toolkit
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether an integrated sorting surface and organized portable storage would be useful in the reader's repair workflow.
emails.next_step_value: The page shows how the toolkit's magnetic case, foam insert, sorting-tray lid, and fabric roll are designed to store and carry the tools.
emails.next_step_limit: The storage design does not identify where each removed screw belongs or eliminate the need to track parts carefully.
emails.subject_strategy: Earn the open with a specific overlooked moment in a repair—what to do with screws after removing them—rather than a generic tool feature.
must_not_reuse: The Pro Tech Toolkit is a fit when the reader wants coverage across several electronics categories and expects projects to require opening, prying, gripping, or anti-static tools as well as screwdriver bits.

emails.job: Resolve the concern that a first general toolkit may not remain dependable beyond a small number of repairs.
emails.single_idea: The Pro Tech Toolkit carries a Lifetime Guarantee that promises covered products will function for as long as the customer has them, with explicit exclusions for misuse, accidental damage, installation damage, device damage, and data loss.
emails.felt_need: If I invest in a general toolkit, I want to know what support exists if a tool fails during intended use.
emails.status_quo: The reader can otherwise judge durability only from product descriptions and materials before purchase.
emails.why_it_fails: Those details do not by themselves define what the seller will do if a covered product stops functioning.
emails.mechanism: The product page identifies the Lifetime Guarantee, while iFixit's official policy defines its duration and distinguishes covered failure from user-caused damage or unintended use.
emails.belief_shift: Before: lifetime coverage may sound like an undefined durability slogan. After: it is a stated promise of function for as long as the customer owns the covered product, bounded by documented exclusions.
must_not_say: Do not describe the guarantee as unconditional replacement of every toolkit item.
Do not imply that the guarantee covers consumables without separate terms.
Do not imply coverage for misuse, loss, accidental damage, installation errors, device damage, or data loss.
Do not present the guarantee as a repair-success guarantee.
Do not invent a discount, deadline, scarcity claim, or cart activity.
emails.objection: I do not want my first general repair toolkit to become a short-lived purchase after only a few projects.
emails.call_to_action: Review the Pro Tech Toolkit and its Lifetime Guarantee label on the product page: https://www.ifixit.com/products/pro-tech-toolkit
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the documented lifetime coverage meaningfully reduces concern about covered tool failure during intended use.
emails.next_step_value: The product page identifies the Pro Tech Toolkit's Lifetime Guarantee, allowing the reader to verify that coverage is attached to this product.
emails.next_step_limit: The product page does not make the guarantee unconditional, cover user-caused device damage, or guarantee that a repair will succeed.
emails.subject_strategy: Address durability directly by distinguishing a defined lifetime promise from an unlimited repair or damage guarantee.
must_not_reuse: The Pro Tech Toolkit is a fit when the reader wants coverage across several electronics categories and expects projects to require opening, prying, gripping, or anti-static tools as well as screwdriver bits.
During disassembly, the inside of the driver-kit lid can serve as a sorting tray for removed fasteners while the case and foam insert keep the toolkit organized.

brief.voice_notes: Use short, practical sentences and confident repair language. Address the reader as “you” without implying personal repair history. Keep each message focused on one decision and describe the product-page CTA specifically.
